events.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) downgraded to out at Miami; Patriots down to three healthy receivers
events.detail: New England downgraded Brown from Questionable to out on Saturday, per the team site, after a knee flare-up cut his Wednesday practice short and he sat out Thursday and Friday. With Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on IR, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Kyle Williams and practice-squad elevation Ryan Miller are the receivers left.
events.so_what: Bench him; this is now a fact rather than a lean. No Patriots receiver left is a confident start, and the quarterback loses his top target, so temper expectations on the passing game this week.

source.label: Patriots.com: Patriots downgrade A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson to out (Oct. 31)

events.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) downgraded to out at Miami; Rhamondre Stevenson in line for a heavy workload
events.detail: Henderson was downgraded to out on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday with an illness, per the Patriots site, which says Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to take a heavy workload with Corey Kiner seeing more snaps. New England signed Lan Larison from the practice squad to fill the gameday spot.
events.so_what: Stevenson becomes a volume FLEX play with goal-line work; the 2-FLEX shape makes a clear lead back in a one-game vacancy worth starting over a thin WR3. Kiner is a deep bench flier only.

source.label: Patriots.com: Patriots downgrade A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson to out (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (turf toe) ruled out for Monday night at Seattle
events.detail: Ben Johnson told reporters Monangai has been ruled out for Week 8, per The Big Lead. He has not practiced since the turf toe and has missed every game since Week 4.
events.so_what: Out is out: he comes out of any Monday slot now, before Sunday locks, so fill it with a Sunday player.

source.label: The Big Lead: Breece Hall, Kyle Monangai and more RB injury updates for Week 8 (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) ruled out for Monday night vs. Chicago
events.detail: Shaheed was ruled out after missing Thursday and Friday practice, per FOX 13's Curtis Crabtree via RotoWire. It is his first missed game of 2026; the knee was hurt in the Week 7 win over Kansas City. Tory Horton and Cooper Kupp are expected to absorb more snaps behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and his next chance is Week 9 vs. Arizona.
events.so_what: Swap him out now with a Sunday player rather than waiting on Monday. Horton gains snaps but is a dart throw, not a start.

source.label: RotoWire: Rashid Shaheed ruled out for MNF (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price cleared, off the injury report for Monday night vs. Chicago
events.detail: Seattle removed both backs from the injury report Saturday, per Rotoworld; each still needs the procedural activation from IR before kickoff. It would be Charbonnet's 2026 debut after his 2025 ACL tear and is expected to come with managed reps, while Price, who upgraded to a full practice Friday, looks like the top option. No snap split has been announced, and Emanuel Wilson's short-term lead role likely ends.
events.so_what: Three backs and no announced split on a Monday night is the worst case for a lineup: bench all of them this week unless you have nothing else, and watch the snap shares to see who owns the role from Week 9.

source.label: Rotoworld: Jadarian Price to return for MNF in Week 8 (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Colts open to trading Jonathan Taylor, with talks active; Josh Downs has already asked out
events.detail: ESPN and NFL Network report Indianapolis is willing to move Taylor and is actively talking with the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants and Seahawks; Taylor has not requested a trade and leads the league with eight rushing TDs (587 yards). Josh Downs asked to be traded earlier this week, and Prime Video's James Palmer reports the Chiefs have been working the phones for a receiver, with Downs among the names. The Colts (2-5) have already dealt Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; the deadline is Nov. 10.
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start until he moves; a trade into a crowded backfield would cost him touches, while a lead-back landing spot keeps the TD equity. Whoever inherits the Colts backfield becomes a speculative stash the day it happens. Downs is a bench hold pending a destination.

source.label: NFL.com: Colts willing to trade RB Jonathan Taylor; talks active, ongoing (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley cleared, no designation for Sunday night at Washington after a limited Friday practice
events.detail: Barkley missed the first two practices of the week with a lingering hamstring and the back injury from Monday's loss to Dallas, then practiced in a limited capacity Friday and carries no designation on the final report. Asked Friday whether he would play, he said "I would hope so." RotoWire expects a heavy workload with the rest of the Eagles backfield banged up. Philadelphia plays at Washington on Sunday night.
events.so_what: This reverses Thursday's read: no designation means he is a start. The risk left is a Sunday night kickoff, so if he is a surprise inactive you learn it after the afternoon slots lock. Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell go back to being handcuffs only.

source.label: RotoWire: Saquon Barkley in clear for Sunday (Oct. 30)

events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out for Sunday night at Washington
events.detail: Smith missed practice all week and is listed as out, per RotoWire; Wicks is also out, so both sit for a second straight game. RotoWire expects Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to handle most of the receiver snaps, with Tanner McKee at quarterback after Jalen Hurts went to IR.
events.so_what: Bench both. The targets spread across four receivers behind a backup quarterback, so none of them is a confident start; Lemon is the name to watch if the snaps concentrate, but not a bid on one game of a rotation.

source.label: RotoWire: DeVonta Smith ruled out for Sunday's game (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Tyjae Spears (knee) ruled out vs. Cincinnati; Calvin Ridley questionable after a full Friday
events.detail: Tennessee's final report lists Tate and Spears as out, per CBS Sports. Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable but was a full participant Friday. RotoWire expects Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike to pick up receiver snaps alongside slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. With Spears out in Week 7, Tony Pollard ran 25 times for 129 yards and three TDs against Cleveland.
events.so_what: Spears out again makes Pollard the whole Titans run game for a second week, an RB2 with touchdown upside. Ridley, full Friday, is the lead receiver if active, but in a weak passing game he is a FLEX at best. Ayomanor is a deep-league stash, not a Tuesday bid on one game.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 8 final injury report (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Lamar Jackson cleared, no designation for Sunday at Buffalo after three full practices
events.detail: Jackson is not listed on Baltimore's final report and will play Sunday at Buffalo after missing three games with a high ankle sprain, per CBS Sports. Tyler Huntley started those three games. Baltimore ruled out guard Vega Ioane and listed RB Adam Randall questionable (neck).
events.so_what: Back in the lineup. His rushing is the premium this format pays a quarterback for, and a 4-point pass TD keeps the passing side from mattering as much as the legs. Huntley is a drop in any league that does not need a bye fill.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 8 final injury report (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice cleared, no designations for Sunday at Denver after full Friday practices
events.detail: Kansas City's final report lists Kelce (ankle) FP/LP/FP and Rice (hamstring, knee) LP/LP/FP, both with no game designation, per A to Z Sports. Rice returns after missing the past two games. Kelce caught four of eight targets for 44 yards last week and has not scored since Week 3.
events.so_what: Both are starts. Rice reclaims the top receiver role, which trims Kelce's target share somewhat, but tight end is shallow enough that Kelce stays in lineups.

source.label: A to Z Sports: Chiefs final injury report for Week 8 vs. Broncos (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) questionable after two limited practices; RJ Harvey (knee) ruled out vs. Kansas City
events.detail: Denver's final report lists Waddle DNP/LP/LP and questionable, and Harvey, a new addition Thursday, did not practice Friday and is out, per A to Z Sports. Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle) went LP/FP/FP and has no designation.
events.so_what: Waddle never got past limited, so he is a genuine coin flip; the 4:25 kickoff lets you check inactives at 1:00 ET, and Courtland Sutton is the safe Denver receiver either way. Harvey out trims Denver's three-back split to two for the week.

source.label: A to Z Sports: Chiefs final injury report for Week 8 vs. Broncos (Oct. 30)

events.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) questionable vs. Baltimore after another week of non-contact practice
events.detail: Moore is questionable for Sunday against the Ravens, per The Buffalo News' Katherine Fitzgerald via RotoWire, after staying limited all week; CBS Sports notes he practiced in a non-contact jersey. He has missed two games and did not play through Questionable tags in Weeks 5 or 6. If he sits, RotoWire expects Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir to take the top snaps.
events.so_what: Same script as the last two Questionable tags, both of which ended in a scratch. Bench him in a 1:00 game where you cannot wait on inactives; Coleman and Shakir split the gain, so neither is a must-start.

source.label: RotoWire: DJ Moore questionable for Week 8 (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) ruled out vs. Atlanta; concussion no longer the issue
events.detail: Egbuka has been ruled out for Sunday against the Falcons with a foot injury, per Scott Smith of the Bucs' official site via RotoWire. His next chance to play is Week 9 against Chicago, and Tampa Bay has its bye the following week. RotoWire expects Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst to take more snaps alongside slot man Chris Godwin.
events.so_what: Out this week, and a Week 9 return then a bye means one game in the next two at best if the foot lingers. Godwin is the Bucs receiver to start; Johnson and Hurst split the rest and neither is worth a bid on a one-week opening.

source.label: RotoWire: Emeka Egbuka ruled out for Week 8 (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) questionable vs. Las Vegas after a third limited practice
events.detail: Hall is questionable for Sunday against the Raiders, per the New York Post's Brian Costello via RotoWire, after being limited Thursday and Friday. He has not played since Week 3. Braelon Allen has been productive in his absence, which RotoWire says leaves the split uncertain if Hall returns.
events.so_what: Never got to a full practice, and last week's similar pattern ended inactive. In a 1:00 game, sit him unless you can afford a zero; if he does play, expect a share with Allen rather than his old workload.

source.label: RotoWire: Breece Hall listed questionable for Sunday (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love cleared, no designation for Sunday at Dallas after a full Friday practice
events.detail: Love (ankle) practiced fully Friday after two limited sessions and carries no designation for Sunday, per ESPN's Josh Weinfuss via RotoWire, which expects close to a normal workload after his two-game absence. Tyler Allgeier (toe) also has no designation. Allgeier and Bam Knight split the backfield nearly evenly the last two weeks; RotoWire expects Knight to return to a rotational role.
events.so_what: This turns Thursday's forecast into a fact: start Love as an RB2 or better. Knight goes back to a handcuff, and Allgeier is a bench hold with Love back.

source.label: RotoWire: Jeremiyah Love ready to return in Week 8 (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase cleared, off the final injury report for Sunday vs. Tennessee
events.detail: Chase (ankle) is off Cincinnati's final report for Sunday against the Titans, per NFL.com's Friday roundup, after a Wednesday rest-and-ankle DNP and a full Thursday. He said he banged the ankle late in the Week 7 win over Baltimore. TE Erick All went to IR this week with a torn ACL.
events.so_what: No designation, so start him as normal; Wednesday was maintenance.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Friday Oct. 30

events.headline: Aaron Jones cleared, no designation for Sunday at Detroit after a full Friday; will share with Jordan Mason
events.detail: Jones (knee) avoided a designation after a full practice Friday, per Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site via RotoWire, which expects him and Jordan Mason to share the backfield, with rookie Demond Claiborne in a depth role. Mason out-snapped Jones 38 to 15 in Week 7, his first game off IR, with 15 carries for 68 yards, before Jones aggravated the MCL sprain he has played through since Week 2.
events.so_what: Jones playing makes this a split, not a takeover in either direction. Mason had the bigger role last week and is the Vikings back to start; Jones is a FLEX-depth play at best on a timeshare.

source.label: RotoWire: Jordan Mason sharing backfield with Jones vs. Detroit (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Ladd McConkey cleared, off the injury report for Sunday vs. the Rams after the concussion protocol
events.detail: McConkey has been removed from the report and will play Sunday against the Rams, per ESPN's Week 8 inactives watch; RotoWire adds that Tre' Harris (hamstring) was also cleared and expects Quentin Johnston's role to shrink slightly. McConkey missed Week 6 with a foot injury before the concussion.
events.so_what: Out of the protocol and undesignated, so he is a start. With both McConkey and Harris back, the Chargers' targets narrow again and Johnston becomes the receiver to be careful with.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 inactives watch (Oct. 30)

events.headline: George Pickens (shoulder, hamstring) questionable vs. Arizona after three limited practices
events.detail: Pickens was limited in all three Cowboys practices this week and is questionable for Sunday against the Cardinals, per RotoWire, though indications are he is expected to play. Dallas kicks off at 1:00 p.m. ET, so his status is settled about 90 minutes before lock.
events.so_what: Lean start: he practiced every day, which is not the pattern of a scratch. The 1:00 kickoff means checking inactives at 11:30 a.m. ET before lineups lock.

source.label: RotoWire: George Pickens questionable for Sunday (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) questionable vs. Indianapolis after a Friday DNP
events.detail: Meyers was limited Wednesday and Thursday out of the bye, then did not practice Friday, and is questionable for Sunday against the Colts, per RotoWire, which says Jacksonville is leaving the light on for him. If he sits, Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would see expanded roles behind Parker Washington.
events.so_what: Going backward to a DNP on Friday is the worrying part. He was a fringe start before the injury; bench him in a 1:00 game rather than wait on inactives.

source.label: RotoWire: Jakobi Meyers questionable for Week 8 (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Christian Watson breaks a rib on a 53-yard catch, returns and finishes with 113 yards in the 27-19 win over Carolina
events.detail: Watson landed on the ball after a 53-yard catch from Jordan Love in the second quarter, was coughing up blood and went to a hospital before halftime, per ESPN's Rob Demovsky. Scans showed a broken rib, but he was cleared and returned in the third quarter, finishing with 8 catches for 113 yards on 10 targets. Green Bay has ten days before its Week 9 game at New England.
events.so_what: He finished the game, and the Thursday kickoff buys ten days of rest, so this is a watch, not a bench. Check his first practice listing next week; a rib fracture is the kind of injury that can carry a designation into game day.

source.label: RotoWire: Christian Watson suffers broken rib Thursday (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Josh Jacobs handles 27 touches and scores twice in his second game back, a workhorse on poor efficiency
events.detail: Jacobs ran 21 times for 39 yards and a 1-yard TD and caught all six targets for 13 yards and a 4-yard TD in Thursday's 27-19 win over Carolina. He made his season debut in Week 7, four days earlier, and his workload rose noticeably. RotoWire reads him as settled into a workhorse role. Green Bay plays at New England on Nov. 8.
events.so_what: The touchdowns carried this line, not the 1.9 yards per carry, but 27 touches plus the goal-line work is the role that matters. He is a start every week he is healthy; the efficiency is a reason to temper expectations, not to bench him.

source.label: RotoWire: Josh Jacobs pair of TDs in primetime win (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand, hamstring) upgraded to full Thursday after a Wednesday rest day; Treylon Burks downgraded to DNP
events.detail: Diggs was listed as a full participant Thursday after sitting Wednesday with a hand and hamstring listing plus rest. Treylon Burks (foot) went from limited to a non-participant. Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Marcus Mariota (knee) were both full. Washington hosts Philadelphia on Sunday night, with Terry McLaurin out for the season on IR.
events.so_what: Full on Thursday turns Wednesday into maintenance. With McLaurin done, Diggs is Washington's target leader; start him unless Friday adds a designation. Burks going backward removes the one other receiver who might have soaked up targets.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Thursday Oct. 29

events.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) a full participant Thursday after a Wednesday DNP; Friday designation still to come
events.detail: Gibbs was a full participant Thursday per Detroit Sports Nation, after sitting Wednesday with a shoulder listing on a day the Lions rested several veterans. He ran 29 times for 116 yards and caught five passes in the win over Green Bay, then said he had aggravated his ankle on the final play; Dan Campbell said he "should be good." Amon-Ra St. Brown, rested Wednesday, was also full Thursday. Detroit hosts Minnesota on Nov. 1.
events.so_what: A full Thursday is the signal that mattered; a bell cow coming off 34 touches stays in the lineup. Only an unexpected Friday designation changes that.

source.label: Detroit Sports Nation: Lions injury report, Oct. 29
